# (2) C1_PARTIAL_INTERVAL -- the digest of the historical RECON03 C1
#                            interval, which for FOR and INV is a
#                            PREFIX of the definition and for CSET
#                            happens to BE the whole definition.
# (3) C2_CLAIMED_RANGE_RECOMPUTED -- the digest actually produced by
# (4) THE RECORDED CLAIM   -- what the historical documents assert.
# PART 2: THE C1 PARTIAL INTERVALS, REPRODUCED EXACTLY
# The C1 digests are VALID for their C1 intervals. They are never
# relabelled as whole-definition digests. For CSET the C1 interval
# COINCIDES with the whole definition (the function is only 152 bytes),
# so the C1 digest IS the whole-function digest there -- a fact the
# historical records never stated, and one this ACT now states
# explicitly rather than leaving it to be misread.

# PART 4: WHAT THE HISTORICAL RECON03 C2 CONTRACT ACTUALLY SAID
# The "35517..36576" notation is INCLUSIVE-ON-BOTH-ENDS as written.
# Under that reading the C2 range covers 1060 bytes, which is one byte
# MORE than the 1059-byte half-open [35517,36576). The C2 contract
# is therefore internally inconsistent about its own convention. This
# ACT does not repair the historical text; it records the ambiguity
# and freezes an explicit, unambiguous convention for the successor.
